title: Kollam Cashew Processors — FIFO process costing
narrative: Kollam Cashew Processors runs a single roasting department that converts shelled cashews into packaged kernels. The department uses a FIFO process-costing system. Materials are added at the start of the process; conversion costs are incurred evenly. Production and cost data for May are set out in Exhibits 1 and 2. There is no spoilage. The Cost Accountant has asked you to compute equivalent units, cost per equivalent unit, and the cost of production report figures the Board pack requires.

tasks.prompt: Under FIFO, calculate equivalent units for materials for May.
tasks.hint: Whole units. Materials are added at the start of the process.
tasks.explanation: Opening WIP already 100% complete for materials, so 0 EU to finish it. Started and completed = 22,000 - 5,000 = 17,000. Ending WIP = 8,000 x 100% = 8,000. EU materials = 0 + 17,000 + 8,000 = 25,000.

tasks.prompt: Under FIFO, calculate equivalent units for conversion for May.
tasks.explanation: To complete opening: 5,000 x (1 - 0.40) = 3,000. Started and completed = 17,000. Ending WIP = 8,000 x 25% = 2,000. EU conversion = 3,000 + 17,000 + 2,000 = 22,000.

tasks.prompt: Complete the statement of cost per equivalent unit (FIFO).

fields.label: Materials cost per equivalent unit is
and conversion cost per equivalent unit is

tasks.explanation: Materials: $200,000 / 25,000 = $8.00. Conversion: $154,000 / 22,000 = $7.00. FIFO uses only costs added this period in the rate calculation.

tasks.prompt: Calculate the total cost of units completed and transferred out in May under FIFO.
tasks.explanation: Opening WIP costs $56,000 + conversion to finish opening 3,000 x $7 = $21,000 + started-and-completed 17,000 x ($8 + $7) = $255,000 = $332,000.

tasks.prompt: Calculate the cost of ending work in process at 31 May.
Classify each statement as true of FIFO process costing, weighted-average process costing, or both.

items.text: Separates work done in the prior period from work done this period
Blends opening WIP costs into the current-period unit cost
Requires a physical-flow reconciliation of units
Computes equivalent units only for work performed this period

tasks.explanation: FIFO isolates prior-period work and costs; weighted average merges opening costs into the unit rate. Both methods begin with a physical-flow (units) reconciliation.

tasks.prompt: If the department had instead used weighted-average costing, which figure would change?

options: Equivalent units for materials and conversion, and therefore cost per EU and the cost assignment
Physical units completed and transferred out
The fact that materials are added at the start of the process

tasks.explanation: Weighted average redefines EU (opening + started work counted together) and folds opening costs into the rate, changing cost per EU and the assignment. Physical completions and total costs to account for are method-independent; material timing is a process fact.
